posts.body: I bought RPG Maker MV a number of years ago. The computer it is on will need to be replaced soon. I no longer have any of the original emails when I purchased an activation code. I've contacted support and they have no record of any of the emails I would've used. I hope I don't have to pay $80.00 for a new code. Anyone have any ideas?

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Where did you purchase it, and which support did you contact?
It is possible you contacted the wrong support team, seeing as GGG is no longer associated with the publisher, and, iirc, the publisher has gone through various name changes.

I mean, we can't tell you anything. You're the one whose been googling things, so you'd have to confirm that on your own end.
I did a generic search just for "RPG Maker" and no other terms, and the result was rpgmakerweb, this website (well, specifically the distribution website. Currently we are speaking on the forums which is part of the website, but I digress).
The standalone version is distributed by Komodo store, so if you haven't tried contacting their support, please try that:
Contact Us
About RPG Maker Questions about RPG Maker tools and the resource packs made by Gotcha Gotcha Games are now handled directly by them. You can find their contact form here: https://rpgmakerofficial.com/en/contactform/ Store For questions related to your order, payment and product delivery, use the...
plaza-us.komodo.jp
They should have record of your purchase, however, if they are saying they
don't
have a record, then you either didn't purchase from this website or provided incorrect information.
Did you perhaps purchase it through Steam?
If so, you simply need to download steam, log in, and it will be in your account library; no need to do any activations.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
even if you didn't purchase through steam you should check your steam library.
because the standalone key always doubled as a steam key, and you might have activated it on steam even if you didn't use it there.
and a few years ago you could only purchase MV either as the standaline on this website or through a steam reseller. GGG wasn't its own company at that time but a programming team of Kadokawa (or however the japanese publisher ofthat time is spelled).
